metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.79

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.79
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.79
- Datum: 01.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 5 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, thanks for your cable, I hope our friends will get the
Argentine visa as the minister in persona was so kind to cable twice to
London; should he go to Argentine he has to pass per Brazil and I shall see him
there and give him every help, also in Buenos Aires my friends will be useful to him.
It is now quasi impossible to get any visas; for Edemann I will try again in Cuba
about a fortnight when Cata's daughter will arrive here. We will have here in the
great hall of the Foreign Office here a memorial-celebration for him on Monday,
presided by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and I will speak there in the name
of his European friends - (in French naturally.) So we are always busy and we have
to ~~keep~~ defend us against too many invitations; I personally don't like not
to leave our room from where we have the most marvellous views in the world
and till now the weather is splendid and not at all hot so that I have even not
yet worn my tropic clothes. - About Eva you have the news from Lotte, that we
have no news at all directly by her. I am nearly convinced that the Salmons do
everything to let her forget her family and to cut off all visits. I am not a
great admirer of my sister in law and would dearly exchange her against one
like you but I must admit that she has tried her best, except with that one letter of Eva a very friendly letter to look after her. Also our-
selves had never a line from Salmons it seems that they like Eva so much that
they will not cease give her bad. In any case we wrote her a energetic letter.
Please do not worry about all that. She is safe, that's what matters. And all
post-war things are so obscure that we better do not to think about - we have
to live this time through and the most important remains to live and to keep
fit for all the nice surprises which are expecting us. - From all our London
friends we have not heard a word, Friedlaender has not yet arrived here
and the only thing he would be useful to me would be to hear about you
and your daily life. I hope that Manfred and you will after the days of
work retire to have some rest at Bath, I cannot repeat too often, that we
want to see you not only in good health but also with good temper
and unshaken nerves. I know how Manfred likes his duty as a doctor,
but a doctor has not only to render healthy his patients but also himself.
Now we have more than one month or two to make our plans, if we

Rückseite des ersten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.

pages.transcription:
About our next plans, Lotte has already written to you,
~ if all goes right we shall be end of January in Newyork
and when this letter arrives you will have our adress - but
you can always write also to my publisher c/o Vikingpress
18 East 48 Street. The voyage will be a hard strain as we have
to be first in Bahia, Recife, Belem on the Amazonas - look at
the map and you will see the distances. From there we will
fly to Miami and from there go by train (30 hours) because
I prefer not to change the climate too quickly from 40° plus
to 20° minus. Yesterday I was surprised by Friedlaender's visit
he is here with wife and child and a "nurse", I have not
spoken him but by telefone and see him tonight. I am plea-
sed that he did not come earlier - how we are leaving alrea-
dy and he can tell his stories to others. He came in the last
moment as I hear that all visas will be stopped. I hope
Friedental got his; the consulate must have not only one
cable about him but two; as the consul refused it first to
Fandhoff who was mentioned in the same cable, he called
again the order for both. All what you say about the new
summer house - beauty in Bath has created mixed feeling
in us, pleasure and the doubt, if we will ever be able to
enjoy such quiet life. But let us not worry about the future
- all I hope is to find a quiet place for the next two or
three month to work and you will have a report about your
daughter. Mail is much quicker from the States than from here.
To America you better send cables with paid reply as we
will be short of cash but I hope that like in Argentine I
will by lectures and articles find easily my way. About a
second lecture tour to South America I shall decide there

Kindest regards to you all from yours Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf rosa Papier. Tinte violett. 'on the' ist über der Zeile eingefügt.
Rückseite des dritten Blattes, durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite sichtbar. Leer.
Rückseite des dritten Blattes mit aufgelegter Farb- und Grauskala zur Archivierung.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der violetten Tinte auf rosa Papier. Die wenigen Einfügungen sind klar als solche erkennbar.
